title: With the lord of the field as a friend

words.context: Bhāskara: «क्षेत्रस्य निष्पत्त्याधारस्य», the ground on which crops are won

words.gram: m. instr. sg. (Vedic पतिना for पत्या)

words.meaning: a friend, one who is kindly disposed
and (Bhāskara); or a preverb ‘hither’ (Sāyaṇa supplies a verb)
words.context: Bhāskara: «आकारस्समुच्चये»; Sāyaṇa on RV 4.57.1: «आ हरत्विति शेषः»

words.meaning: may he be gracious, make happy
words.role: main verb of the second sentence

sandhi.rule: u before a vowel becomes v

morphology.note: the old ending -masi of the first person plural (for -maḥ); Bhāskara cites P. 7.1.46 (इदन्तो मसि).
subjunctive with the vowel -ā- (leṭ), said as a wish; Bhāskara: «लेटोऽडाटौ»

translation.literal: With the lord of the field, as with a friend, we win cow, horse, nourishment; may he be gracious to us in such [a matter].
translation.readable: With the Lord of the Field as our friend we win cattle and horses and food that makes us thrive; may he be kind to us in all of this.

units.pause_note: Both Taittirīya witnesses keep नः unjoined before मृडाति (where sandhi would give नो), and the vākya-krama text marks a pause there (स नः॑ ॥ मृ॒डा॒ती॒दृशे॑): the verse is divided at that pause.

meaning: A verse to Kṣetrapati, the lord of the field — the divinity of cultivated land. With his help, as with a friend’s, the sacrificers win cattle, horses and nourishing food, and they ask him to be gracious in it. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (1.1.14) it stands among the verses for the optional iṣṭis (kāmyeṣṭi), followed by its companion kṣetrasya pate; it is also Ṛgveda 4.57.1. Sāyaṇa on the Ṛgveda notes that some take the lord of the field to be Rudra, others Agni, others a deity of his own. The use of the verse for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition, not to the Veda: in its source it serves another rite (see the commentary).
in_the_rite: The third mantra of Aṅgāraka’s step in the Navagraha sūktam, naming Kṣetrapati. S names the adhidevatā and pratyadhidevatā together in the salutation that follows, without saying which mantra is whose.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara: «क्षेत्रस्य निष्पत्त्याधारस्य, पतिना पत्याऽधिष्ठात्रा»; «यथा हितेन मित्रेण जनेन अमित्रं जयति एवं क्षेत्रपतिना जयेम»; and «स च क्षेत्रपतिः नोस्मान् मृडाति मृडयतु सुखयतु».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa on RV 4.57.1 quotes a verse on who the lord of the field is: «रुद्रं क्षेत्रपतिं प्राहुः केचिदग्निमथापरे», and takes हितेनेव as «सर्वप्राणिहितेनैव तेन. अथवा मित्रेणेव».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: The Taittirīya text writes स नः मृडाती॑दृशे, and the second witness marks a pause after नः (स नः॑ ॥); the Ṛgveda (4.57.1) joins it as स नो मृळाती॒दृशे॑.
